decision: Corrected eng review: G1 is two nutrient-name constants plus reconciliation, not a chemistry rule
rationale: Measured against the live FDC API after egress was opened. Gate passes 0/11 under current code. Cause is name drift (Glucose vs Glucose (dextrose), Total Sugars vs Sugars, Total NLEA), not galactose coverage. Reconciling the breakdown against Total Sugars supersedes the hardcoded safely-zero sugar list.

decision: Ship v0.5.0 (MINOR); keep package.json as the single version source, no VERSION file
rationale: USDA import went from never populating PAC/POD/Sugar to populating them for most ingredients -- new working capability, backward compatible. Declined the 4-digit VERSION file because package.json is already the project version of record and a second file is a second source of truth. Known consequence: gstack version tooling reports DRIFT_UNEXPECTED on this repo.

decision: Batch loop re-sequenced: Phase 0 prerequisites (serializer, canonical save, copy identity, print snapshot, test lane) block all feature work
rationale: Cross-model review found three capabilities the design assumed exist and do not. Save rebuilds the container as {Recipe, Ingredients} (recipe-manager.js:1195) and load copies only keys already on a fresh cRecipe (app.js:284), so any added field is silently dropped on round-trip. Print is a bare window.print() (recipe-manager.js:1400) that emits the live DOM including unsaved edits, so a QR could resolve to a formula never saved. copyFrom is Object.assign (core.js:108) so copy would clone a stable id. All verified independently. Also adds a batch record entity distinct from recipe, since a version can be churned repeatedly.

decision: P0.5: recipe containers are detached, deeply frozen snapshots built by one canonical path; library load extracted to its own module
rationale: buildRecipeContainer returned a view onto the live recipe while the cloud write is fire-and-forget: google-drive-storage.saveRecipe awaits findFileByName before updateFile stringifies, so edits made in that window entered the cloud copy while IndexedDB held the earlier state -- two backends disagreeing with no error and no attribution. Fixed by returning deepFreeze(structuredClone(container)) from one builder (snapshotForSave in recipe-manager.js), used by both library save and .ier export. Frozen as well as detached because detaching alone is a convention a later caller can break; module code is strict so a late write throws at the offending line. deepFreeze guards on isFrozen because structuredClone preserves cycles. structuredClone refuses functions and DOM nodes that JSON.stringify used to drop silently -- that refusal is reported via ErrorMsg rather than rethrown, since an uncaught throw in the async save handler is an unhandled rejection (the user clicks Save and nothing happens). Cloning drops prototypes, which matches what every reader already saw since both backends round-trip through JSON or a structured clone. Also closed review item 16: app.js onLoad moved to js/features/recipe-library-load.js as createLibraryRecipeLoader(deps) so the refusal-gate ORDER is testable; the .ier-import-vs-library-load backup divergence was reviewed and KEPT deliberately, since aligning it is a user-visible change and Phase 0 is structural only.

decision: P0.3 identity: in-container behind SchemaVersion 2 (RecipeId + SavedAt); index dropped; P0.6 guards merged into the cut; sync joins id-first with name fallback via pure extracted module
rationale: One Drive file is the only atomic unit (updateFile media-PATCH, google-drive-storage.js:431); a separate identity store forks ids on ordinary partial sync. Mint on save only (never load) prevents the migration fork. Outside voice caught: id-first join cannot see ids in listRecipes output so the join downloads bodies; save-as-new-name in the mainline flow duplicates ids unless copy-mints/overwrite-reprompt guards ship WITH the writer; the local index rebuilt blocker-2 resurrection inside the mitigation so it is deferred to P0.4; updatedAt is re-stamped at write time so SavedAt (author clock) travels in the v2 container. Pre-P0.2 strip threat closed operationally: reload every device at rollout, verify cache-busting. v2 with missing id loads-with-warning and re-mints on save; validation lives OUTSIDE containerProblem.

decision: Decision 6 AMENDED (T2.5, cross-model KEEP verdict): a save mints when keeping the id would put it on two local records; otherwise identity follows the recipe
rationale: Codex and Claude independently recommended KEEP for the confirmed different-id overwrite when nothing else carries the incoming id (the .ier import-collision case). Minting there protects nothing -- the target record's identity dies with its record either way -- while costing the surviving recipe its batch-history attachment and making the future id-first sync join manufacture duplicates instead of converging. The original letter was written about the rename-copy flow, where minting is genuinely required. Honest cost recorded: the id a save produces depends on a local scan, not predictable from the prompt alone.

decision: Decision 14: sync legacy conflicts REJECT outright — graft-with-warning withdrawn (maintainer, N=1 scope call)
rationale: For an app with one user, merge semantics for old-format-vs-identified collisions are not worth design time. An id-less body never replaces an identified record (SYNC_WARNINGS.LEGACY_CONFLICT in both planRecipeSync and decideRecipePush); handled on an exception basis via the warning. The identified-winner direction stays open so old records get carried forward, and scripts/migrate-legacy-recipes.js (throwaway) drains the legacy population. Accepted cost: a genuinely-newer legacy edit stalls until a human re-saves it. Remaining codex P2s banked, not designed around.

decision: P0.4 batch schema: a batch is a churn event, created AT PRINT in state planned; no-verdict is a value; ingredient order not meaningful so the diff is keyed by name; prose return path and defect taxonomy both CUT
rationale: Binder audit of 29 churned pages: 14 produced no result and silence is ambiguous, so outcome-time record creation reproduces the holes. Six of ten changes that altered the next batch came from prose, so the open field is where diagnoses live rather than a taxonomy.

decision: PR #11 merged as squash 644a598; branch restarted from main. Banked findings triaged by redesign disposition; the 11 REDESIGN-INDEPENDENT ones filed as issues #19-#24 grouped by root cause
rationale: The UI/UX replacement is about to become the focus, and a pending-todo file on a superseded branch is exactly how work gets orphaned. Grouping by root cause avoids the issue-per-step rot CLAUDE.md warns about.

decision: P0.4 schema needs revision before B1 starts — codex consult returned GATE FAIL with 13 P1s. Do not implement against the current text.
rationale: Four findings verified against the repo: the name-keyed diff collapses duplicate ingredient rows (design:455 already recorded this failure mode), the marks schema collapses flavor quality and intensity (audit:94 explicitly warns against it), SavedAt is absent though decision 22 syncs batches on it, and P0.4 never answers what happens to batches when a recipe is deleted (design:536).
